problem:
A total of $2$ milliliters of water evaporate from a beaker every second.
What differential equation describes the rate of change of the amount of water $W$ (in milliliters) remaining in the beaker?  Assume that the time $t$ is measured in seconds.

feedback.worked_solution:
If the number of enrollments is $E,$ then the rate of change of the number of enrollments is $\frac{\text{d}E}{\text{d}t},$ where $t$ is the time in hours.

Since $18$ new enrollments are added every hour, the rate of change of the number of enrollments is given by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}E}{\text{d}t}=18.
$$
